title: Engine Failed To Start
shortDescription: Hybrid powertrain failed to crank or start the internal combustion engine.
fullDescription:
P0A0F sets when the hybrid control module commands the ICE to start (typically via the motor/generator MG1) but RPM and combustion are not confirmed within the calibrated time window. The vehicle may continue in EV mode if HV battery is sufficient, or it may go into a reduced-power 'limp home' state.

Common root causes include a weak HV battery (cannot supply cranking current to MG1), a fault in the inverter/converter assembly, low fuel pressure, ignition system failure, or an MG1 resolver/position-sensor fault. On Toyota/Lexus hybrids this DTC very frequently appears alongside misfire codes when one or more spark plugs or coils have failed.

Diagnosis requires a hybrid-capable scan tool to view MG1/MG2 RPM data, HV battery state-of-charge, and inverter current draw during a start attempt.
safetyImpact: Vehicle may strand the driver. HV system inspection requires high-voltage safety procedures (insulated gloves, service plug removal).

causes.cause: Weak or failing HV battery pack
Failed ignition coil or spark plug
Low fuel pressure or failed fuel pump

fixSteps.title: Scan all modules
fixSteps.instruction: Pull DTCs from PCM, hybrid control, battery ECU, and skid control with hybrid-capable scan tool.

fixSteps.title: Check HV battery health
fixSteps.instruction: View block voltages and internal resistance. Replace pack or weak module if delta exceeds spec.

fixSteps.title: Inspect ignition and fuel
fixSteps.instruction: Test coils, plugs, and fuel pressure. Address any companion misfire DTCs first.

faq.a: No. Tow to a hybrid-qualified shop; HV system service requires PPE and training.

title: Generator Control Module
shortDescription: Internal fault detected in the generator (MG1) control module.
fullDescription:
P0A1A indicates the inverter/generator control module has detected an internal logic, supply, or power-stage fault. The hybrid system will typically force the vehicle into a fail-safe mode, disabling generator function which prevents engine cranking and high-voltage charging of the traction battery.

Failures are often caused by IGBT module breakdown inside the inverter assembly, coolant intrusion, or loss of low-voltage supply to the gate-drive board.

Replacement of the inverter assembly typically follows confirmation that LV power, ground, and CAN are good.
safetyImpact: Vehicle may shut down unexpectedly. HV inverter contains lethal voltage even after key off until capacitors discharge.

fixSteps.title: Confirm LV supply
fixSteps.instruction: Verify 12V power and ground at inverter LV connector with key on.

fixSteps.title: Check inverter coolant
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect dedicated inverter cooling loop level and pump operation.

fixSteps.title: Replace inverter assembly
fixSteps.instruction: Follow OEM HV-safe service procedure: remove service plug, wait capacitor discharge, then swap inverter.

faq.a: No. HV inverter replacement requires certified PPE and procedures.

title: Drive Motor A Control Module
shortDescription: Internal fault in drive motor (MG2) control module.
fullDescription:
P0A1B sets when the inverter section that drives the traction motor (MG2) reports an internal fault. The vehicle will lose propulsion or enter severely reduced-power mode because MG2 is the primary drive motor on most planetary-split hybrids.

Like P0A1A, this is usually an inverter-side failure (IGBT, gate driver, current sensor) and not typically a wiring fault.
safetyImpact: Sudden loss of drive propulsion possible.

fixSteps.title: Scan freeze frame
fixSteps.instruction: Capture conditions; check for companion P0A78/P0A7A.

fixSteps.title: Inverter replacement
fixSteps.instruction: OEM HV procedure required.

faq.a: Will return immediately; system must be repaired.

title: Motor Electronics Coolant Pump Control Circuit
shortDescription: Open or short detected in the inverter coolant pump control circuit.
fullDescription:
P0A1C indicates the hybrid control module cannot drive the dedicated electric coolant pump used to cool the inverter and drive motors. Without flow, the inverter will overheat and derate within minutes of operation.

Most frequent on Toyota Prius generations 2-4 where the inverter pump (Aisin) fails. Also caused by blown fuse, broken pigtail, or seized pump motor.
safetyImpact: Inverter overheat can cause sudden power loss.

fixSteps.title: Check fuse
fixSteps.instruction: Verify HV/inverter pump fuse (often labeled WTR PMP or HEV).

fixSteps.title: Power test pump
fixSteps.instruction: Apply 12V directly to pump to confirm operation.

fixSteps.title: Replace pump
fixSteps.instruction: Drain inverter loop, swap pump, refill and bleed using scan-tool routine.

faq.a: Inverter coolant pump replacement; common Prius failure.

title: Hybrid Powertrain Control Module Internal
shortDescription: Internal hybrid powertrain control module fault detected.
fullDescription:
P0A1D sets when the master hybrid control module fails internal self-tests (RAM/ROM/processor). The fault is in the module itself, not in sensors or wiring.

Unlikely to be a wiring issue. Software flash or module replacement (with programming) is generally required.

fixSteps.title: Check for TSBs
fixSteps.instruction: Search OEM bulletins for reflash availability.

fixSteps.title: Replace and program
fixSteps.instruction: Install new module, perform OEM key/immobilizer init.

title: Battery Energy Control Module
shortDescription: Internal fault in the HV battery energy control module.
fullDescription:
P0A1E indicates the battery ECU has failed an internal self-check. This module monitors block voltages, current, temperature, and SOC for the traction battery.

When lost, the hybrid control module cannot trust battery data and disables HV operation.
safetyImpact: HV system disabled; loss of propulsion possible.

fixSteps.title: Inspect connector
fixSteps.instruction: Open battery service cover, inspect ECU connector for corrosion.

fixSteps.title: Replace ECU
fixSteps.instruction: Swap battery ECU; perform initialization.

faq.a: No, this is HV battery management.

title: Battery Energy Control Module Performance
shortDescription: Battery energy control module is reporting implausible data.
fullDescription:
P0A1F is set when the battery ECU outputs values that conflict with other sensor inputs (for example, claiming high SOC while actual current draw is low or vice versa). The hybrid control rejects the battery ECU output and stores this DTC.

Most commonly caused by current sensor zero-point drift, contaminated ECU, or end-of-life battery pack imbalance.
safetyImpact: Possible reduced power; HV may shut down.

fixSteps.title: Run battery health test
fixSteps.instruction: Use OEM scan tool to capture block voltages and current sensor zero offset.

fixSteps.title: Recalibrate / replace
fixSteps.instruction: Reset zero-point if procedure exists; otherwise replace ECU or pack.

faq.a: Will return; underlying drift must be corrected.

title: Boost Converter Module
shortDescription: Internal fault in the boost (step-up) converter.
fullDescription:
P0A25 sets when the DC-DC step-up (boost) converter that raises HV battery voltage to motor-bus voltage (typically 500-650V) reports an internal fault. Without boost, drive motor torque is severely limited.

Usually fails as part of inverter assembly on Toyota/Ford hybrids; on Honda IMA, may be a discrete unit.

fixSteps.title: Inspect inverter coolant
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm cooling system functional.

fixSteps.title: Replace converter
fixSteps.instruction: Inverter/converter assembly replacement under HV-safe procedure.

faq.a: Often integrated in the same assembly.

title: Boost Converter Module Performance
shortDescription: Boost converter output not within expected range.
fullDescription:
P0A26 sets when the boosted bus voltage doesn't match the commanded value under load. Could be a feedback sensor issue or actual converter underperformance.

Diagnose with hybrid scan tool comparing commanded vs actual VL (low) and VH (high) voltages.

fixSteps.title: Compare commanded vs actual
fixSteps.instruction: Capture bus voltage data under load.

fixSteps.title: Replace inverter
fixSteps.instruction: If converter underperforming, swap assembly.

title: Boost Converter Module Voltage High
shortDescription: Boost converter output voltage above maximum threshold.
fullDescription:
P0A27 sets when the high-side bus voltage exceeds safe limits. The hybrid control immediately disables the boost stage to prevent capacitor or motor insulation damage.

Causes include sensor offset, runaway IGBT switching, or regen-event overshoot due to failed clamp.

fixSteps.title: Replace inverter
fixSteps.instruction: Cannot service in field; replace assembly.

title: Boost Converter Module Voltage Low
shortDescription: Boost converter output voltage below minimum threshold.
fullDescription:
P0A28 sets when the high bus voltage drops below the level needed to drive MG1/MG2 effectively. Usually indicates a converter switching failure, blown HV fuse internal to the inverter, or open boost reactor.

Result is severe power reduction or no-drive.

fixSteps.title: Replace inverter
fixSteps.instruction: Replacement under HV-safe procedure.

title: Boost Converter Temperature Sensor Circuit
shortDescription: Open or short in the boost converter temperature sensor circuit.
fullDescription:
P0A29 indicates the temperature sensor monitoring the boost converter has an out-of-range signal. Without temperature data, the hybrid control derates power as a safety measure.

The sensor is typically internal to the inverter assembly, so repair often requires inverter replacement.

fixSteps.title: Replace inverter
fixSteps.instruction: Sensor not serviceable separately on most platforms.

title: Hybrid Battery Pack Cooling Fan 1 Control Circuit
shortDescription: Open or short detected in HV battery cooling fan control circuit.
fullDescription:
P0A30 indicates the battery ECU cannot drive the HV battery pack cooling fan. NiMH and Li-ion packs require active airflow to keep cells in their optimum temperature window. A failed fan will eventually cause thermal derate or a more serious battery fault.

Very common on older Prius/Camry hybrids where the rear cabin air intake gets clogged with debris and the fan motor seizes.

fixSteps.title: Inspect intake
fixSteps.instruction: Remove rear seat trim, check intake screen and fan blades for debris/pet hair.

fixSteps.title: Test fan
fixSteps.instruction: Apply 12V to fan; replace if dead.

faq.a: Often yes; clean intake first before replacing fan.

title: Hybrid Battery Pack Cooling Fan 1 Control Circuit Low
shortDescription: Battery cooling fan circuit voltage low.
fullDescription:
P0A31 indicates the fan control line is shorted to ground or stuck low. The fan may run continuously or not at all depending on circuit topology.

Usually a chafed harness or shorted fan motor.

fixSteps.title: Resistance test fan
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect fan, measure motor resistance.

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Look for chafing along seat rail.

title: Hybrid Battery Pack Cooling Fan 1 Control Circuit High
shortDescription: Battery cooling fan control circuit voltage high.
fullDescription:
P0A32 sets when the fan control line is open or shorted to power. ECU detects the line not pulling low when commanded.

Usually open wire or unplugged fan connector.

fixSteps.title: Inspect connector
fixSteps.instruction: Verify fan plugged in.

fixSteps.title: Continuity check
fixSteps.instruction: Test wire from battery ECU to fan.

title: Drive Motor A Inverter Temperature Sensor Circuit
shortDescription: Open or short in MG2 inverter temperature sensor.
fullDescription:
P0A38 indicates the MG2 inverter temperature sensor is reporting out-of-range. Without thermal data, the system derates motor power preemptively.

Sensor typically internal to inverter; replacement of full assembly often required.

fixSteps.title: Replace inverter
fixSteps.instruction: Sensor integrated.

title: Drive Motor A Position Sensor Circuit
shortDescription: MG2 resolver position sensor circuit fault.
fullDescription:
P0A40 indicates the resolver (rotary position sensor) for the drive motor MG2 has a circuit fault. The hybrid control needs accurate rotor position to commutate the AC motor; without it, no torque can be produced.

Resolvers rarely fail outright; usually wiring or connector at the motor housing.

fixSteps.title: Inspect connector
fixSteps.instruction: Check resolver connector at transaxle for moisture/corrosion.

fixSteps.title: Resistance test
fixSteps.instruction: Verify resolver coils per OEM spec.

title: Drive Motor A Phase U Current
shortDescription: Drive motor MG2 phase U current out of range.
fullDescription:
P0A60 indicates the U-phase current measurement for MG2 is abnormal. Could be a current sensor failure or actual motor winding problem.

Commonly accompanied by P0A61 (phase V) or P0A62 (phase W) if it's a sensor common to all phases.

fixSteps.title: Insulation test motor
fixSteps.instruction: Megger phase-to-ground.

fixSteps.title: Replace inverter or motor
fixSteps.instruction: Per test result.

title: Drive Motor A Phase V Current
shortDescription: Drive motor MG2 phase V current out of range.
fullDescription:
P0A61 indicates the V-phase current sensor or measurement for drive motor MG2 is reporting an implausible value. Like P0A60, requires distinguishing sensor vs winding fault.

Diagnosis flow identical to P0A60.

fixSteps.title: Insulation test
fixSteps.instruction: Megger.

fixSteps.title: Replace assembly
fixSteps.instruction: Inverter or motor.

title: Drive Motor A Phase W Current
shortDescription: Drive motor MG2 phase W current out of range.
fullDescription:
P0A62 indicates the W-phase current measurement is out of range. Companion DTC to P0A60/P0A61.

If all three set together, the high-side current sensor or shunt is the most likely culprit.

fixSteps.title: Megger test
fixSteps.instruction: Insulation test phase-to-ground.

fixSteps.title: Replace per result
fixSteps.instruction: Motor or inverter.

title: Drive Motor A Phase U-V-W Performance
shortDescription: Generic motor phase performance fault.
fullDescription:
P0A6F is a summary code set when the inverter cannot maintain commanded torque due to phase-related anomalies that don't match a single sensor DTC.

Usually accompanies more specific phase codes; address those first.

fixSteps.title: Address companion DTCs
fixSteps.instruction: Fix specific phase codes first.

title: Replace Hybrid Battery Pack
shortDescription: HV battery deterioration; pack replacement required.
fullDescription:
P0A80 is the canonical 'your hybrid battery is worn out' code. The battery ECU has detected one or more cell modules outside acceptable internal-resistance or capacity limits. SOC will swing wildly and the system will run the ICE far more often than designed.

Options: replace full pack (OEM, costly), replace individual weak modules (requires diagnostic to identify the bad cells), or install a refurbished/aftermarket pack with warranty.

Very common on Toyota Prius gen 2/3 (2004-2015) at 150-200k miles.
safetyImpact: Reduced fuel economy and performance; not immediately unsafe.

fixSteps.title: Battery diagnostic
fixSteps.instruction: Use OEM or hybrid-specialty tool to capture per-block voltage and internal resistance.

fixSteps.title: Module or pack replacement
fixSteps.instruction: Replace identified weak modules with matched-capacity units, or install refurbished pack.

fixSteps.title: Reset and learn
fixSteps.instruction: Clear codes; drive cycle to confirm SOC stability.

faq.q: How long can I drive with this?
faq.a: Will continue functioning but with poor MPG; replace within months to avoid stranding.

title: Hybrid Battery Pack Cooling Fan 2
shortDescription: Secondary battery pack cooling fan circuit fault.
fullDescription:
P0A81 indicates a fault on the second cooling fan used in larger HV battery packs (some Lexus/Highlander hybrids).

Diagnosis follows the same flow as P0A30: clean intake, verify power, replace fan if seized.

fixSteps.title: Verify fuse and connector
fixSteps.instruction: Check power supply.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan
fixSteps.instruction: If dead.

title: Hybrid Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit
shortDescription: Open or short in HV battery voltage-sense wire.
fullDescription:
P0A8E indicates the battery ECU cannot read one of its block voltage sense wires. These run from each cell-module tap to the ECU board.

Frequent failure mode is a single broken or corroded sense wire inside the pack.

fixSteps.title: Open battery pack
fixSteps.instruction: HV-safe procedure; locate the open sense wire by ECU pinout.

fixSteps.title: Repair or replace harness
fixSteps.instruction: Splice or replace ribbon harness.

faq.a: No, but ignored leads to imbalance.

title: Drive Motor A Performance
shortDescription: Drive motor MG2 not delivering commanded torque.
fullDescription:
P0A90 sets when the actual MG2 output torque (calculated from current and back-EMF) doesn't match commanded value over a sustained window. Could be motor winding partial-short, magnet weakening (rare), or inverter calibration drift.

Diagnosis is involved; OEM scan-tool data and bench tests usually required.

fixSteps.title: Capture data
fixSteps.instruction: Compare commanded vs measured torque under load.

fixSteps.title: Replace assembly
fixSteps.instruction: Motor or inverter as indicated.

faq.a: Usually prior overheating; pack ages all parts together.

title: Inverter A Cooling System Performance
shortDescription: Inverter cooling system not maintaining target temperature.
fullDescription:
P0A93 sets when the inverter coolant temperature rises faster or higher than expected for the load condition. Indicates marginal cooling: weak pump, low coolant level, or air pocket in the loop.

Very common after pump replacement if not bled correctly.

fixSteps.title: Top up coolant
fixSteps.instruction: Inverter loop is separate from engine; use spec coolant.

fixSteps.title: Bleed loop
fixSteps.instruction: Run scan-tool bleed routine or follow OEM bleed procedure.

fixSteps.title: Test pump flow
fixSteps.instruction: Pinch return hose to feel flow; replace pump if weak.

faq.a: Different loop; this is dedicated inverter cooling.

title: DC/DC Converter Performance
shortDescription: Auxiliary 14V DC-DC converter not maintaining output.
fullDescription:
P0A94 sets when the DC-DC converter (steps HV down to ~14V to charge the 12V auxiliary battery and run accessories) is underperforming. Symptoms include 12V battery going flat, accessories cutting out at idle, and eventually no-start.

The DC-DC is part of the inverter assembly on most hybrids.

fixSteps.title: Test 12V battery
fixSteps.instruction: Load test; replace if below 12V resting.

fixSteps.title: Measure DC-DC output
fixSteps.instruction: Should be 13.5-14.5V at terminals with vehicle Ready.

fixSteps.title: Replace inverter
fixSteps.instruction: If output low, inverter assembly replacement.

faq.a: Try first; if DC-DC fails to recharge, deeper repair needed.

title: Hybrid Battery Temperature Sensor A Circuit
shortDescription: Open or short in HV battery temperature sensor.
fullDescription:
P0A9C sets when one of the multiple temperature sensors inside the HV battery pack is reporting out-of-range. Without good thermal data, the battery ECU cannot manage cooling fan and SOC limits.

Sensors are typically thermistors mounted to specific cell modules.

fixSteps.title: Identify sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Per OEM pinout in battery ECU.

fixSteps.title: Test resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Check thermistor at known temperature.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: HV-safe procedure to access pack interior.

title: Hybrid Battery System Voltage High
shortDescription: HV battery pack voltage exceeds upper limit.
fullDescription:
P0AC0 sets when total pack voltage rises above the calibrated maximum. Often happens during heavy regenerative braking if a pack module is not accepting charge properly, causing the rest of the pack to over-shoot.

If paired with P0A80, replace pack/modules.

fixSteps.title: Block voltage scan
fixSteps.instruction: Find weakest/strongest module.

fixSteps.title: Module replacement
fixSteps.instruction: Address imbalance.

title: Hybrid Battery System Voltage Low
shortDescription: HV battery pack voltage below lower limit.
fullDescription:
P0AC1 sets when total pack voltage drops below safe minimum during high-current discharge. Indicates one or more very weak modules.

Usually accompanies P0A80 and signals end-of-life pack.

fixSteps.title: Block voltage scan
fixSteps.instruction: Identify weak modules.

fixSteps.title: Replace pack/modules
fixSteps.instruction: OEM or refurb.

faq.a: External charging not standard on hybrids; pack must be repaired.
